dedupe_keys.name: contaminated land from oil spills in the niger delta mapped with planetscope vegetation indices and machine learning environmental monitoring and assessment 2025

description: This case study is a 2025 article in Environmental Monitoring and Assessment by researchers at the University of Glasgow on detecting and measuring land contaminated by oil spills in the Niger Delta, a major oil-producing region where monitoring is limited by slow response, access and safety. The authors use geospatial cloud computing and machine learning on PlanetScope satellite data, deriving six vegetation health indices and analysing them with slow moving average regression, which shows significant declines in vegetation health after spill events between 2016 and 2023. A random forest classifier then quantifies contaminated land: about 4 percent, or 1,180 hectares, of the studied area across vegetation, wetland, farmland and grassland covers. Access: the article is open access in PubMed Central under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence; PlanetScope imagery is commercial and the article page does not offer the processed data. Coverage is the Niger Delta for 2016 to 2023. Caveats: only the abstract and front matter were read, and accuracy figures are in the full text. It suits hazard exposure and post-event analysis studies of oil infrastructure spills, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

name: Contaminated land from oil spills in the Niger Delta mapped with PlanetScope vegetation indices and machine learning (Environmental Monitoring and Assessment, 2025)
outcomes: Vegetation health indices from PlanetScope imagery declined significantly after oil spill events between 2016 and 2023, with Spearman correlations from -0.68 to -0.82, and a random forest classifier estimated that contaminated vegetation, wetland, farmland and grassland cover about 4 percent, or 1,180 hectares, of the Niger Delta area studied.
